existing_programme.title: Lift qualified audit opinion (KPMG LLP)
existing_programme.rationale: External auditor issued a qualified opinion on 2024/25 statements. Direct: PSAA scale fee normalisation. Indirect: lifting governance flag reduces borrowing-cost premium. Manual read of audit report needed to itemise qualification reason — once known, target single-cycle remediation.

existing_programme.title: Energy procurement via CCS / LASER / NEPO frameworks (£1M baseline)
existing_programme.rationale: £1M utility spend across 1 suppliers. Top: EDF ENERGY 1 LTD (£1M). Crown Commercial RM6306 + LASER / NEPO consortium flex purchase typically saves 4-8% vs direct supplier contracts on a 3-yr horizon. Plus solar PV self-generation on council estate (7-9 yr payback) + DESNZ Public Sector Decarbonisation Scheme grants up to 100% capex on heat pump conversion.

existing_programme.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (84 notices; 0 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
existing_programme.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 84 notices (45 awarded, £13M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 0 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £0M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: . Matched against ledger: GB-Lyme: TPPL Newcastle-under-Lyme Borough Council — ceiling £0.0M, actual ledger spend with awardee £0.2M; GB-Lyme: TPPL Newcastle-Under-Lyme Borough Council — ceiling £2.7M, actual ledger spend with awardee £2.8M; GB-Lyme: TPPL Newcastle-Under-Lyme Borough Council — ceiling £0.7M, actual ledger spend with awardee £2.8M. Aggregate identified actual spend £35M. SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.

existing_programme.title: Rebuild general reserves to ≥4 months (Low → Adequate)
existing_programme.rationale: Reserves at 4.0 months (Low per CIPFA Resilience benchmark). Direction: improving. A 4-month minimum is the CIPFA / S151 prudence floor; below this triggers external auditor VFM concern and elevates s.114 risk.

existing_programme.title: Audit + recover £0M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
existing_programme.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £0M across 8 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

additional_opportunities.name: HNSG Local SEND Reform Plan submission — 90% DSG write-off
additional_opportunities.lever_description: Government announced 9 Feb 2026 (alongside final 2026/27 LGFS) that 90% of every English council's accumulated DSG deficit at 31 March 2026 will be written off via a new Section 31 grant — the High Needs Stability Grant (HNSG), worth ~£5.6Bn nationally. Conditional on the council submitting an approved Local SEND Reform Plan to DfE by **19 June 2026**; grants paid Autumn 2026. Safety Valve programme closed 1 April 2026 (folded into HNSG). Statutory override extended to 31 March 2028; gov committed to absorb ALL DSG deficits from 1 April 2028. New 2026/27 + 2027/28 deficits NOT yet covered — linked to demonstrable delivery on approved reform plan (OBR forecast: £8.6Bn additional deficits over those two years).
additional_opportunities.council_specific_rationale: Residual 10% management — plan submission unlocks 90% auto write-off

case_studies.horizon: Autumn 2026 grant; conditional on 19 June 2026 plan submission
case_studies.note: £67.7M deficit → ~£60.9M write-off, ~£6.8M residual. Not previously a Safety Valve participant.
£17M → ~£15.3M write-off, ~£1.7M residual. 2026/27-2028/29 budget approved on HNSG assumption.
Active Safety Valve participant 2022-23 cohort. £17.8M → ~£14.4M HNSG write-off, ~£1.6M residual after SV local contributions count toward 10%.
~£180M at 31 Mar 2026 → ~£162M write-off, ~£18M residual. Not Safety Valve. Reform UK took control 8 May 2026 — plan submission is most material early decision.
